page: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by the QEMU hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC processor family running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 31.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 360 GB NVMe SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included in the base configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the cpx51 demonstrates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test places the instance in the bottom 10% with a score of 771.59, reflecting the shared nature of the vCPUs and the conservative 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12463.46 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8903.0. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the middle 50% tier, registering 86.13 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.91 GB/sec for large-block writes.

This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can tolerate shared CPU resources, such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 18.81 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 12861.66 on PassMark. It also handles light AI tasks, processing 135M parameter LLM prompts at 1214.19 tokens/sec. However, the weak single-core performance and text processing metrics, scoring in the bottom 25% on Geekbench text processing, make it less suitable for single-threaded, latency-sensitive applications. The shared CPU allocation offers a cost-efficient resource density for parallelized, non-critical background jobs and development environments.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx51 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 16 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 31.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 360 GB NVMe SSD. Operating under the QEMU hypervisor, this instance delivers a balanced resource profile for multi-threaded applications despite its shared CPU allocation. Benchmark data reveals a significant performance tradeoff: single-core CPU execution is limited, scoring in the bottom 10% on stress-ng, whereas multi-core performance and memory bandwidth consistently reach average tiers. The server achieves a static web serving throughput of 18.81 GB/sec and processes 30.41 million Redis SET operations per second. This profile makes the cpx51 a cost-effective option for parallelized workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that do not require dedicated CPU cores.
